test_title: PYST 22: SSC JE EE- General Awareness (Held on: 14 Nov 2022 Shift 2)
subject: gk
question:
Consider the following statements related to shuttler Kidambi Srikanth:

1. He won the silver medal at the BWF World Championship 2021.

2. He has been conferred with Arjuna award in 2018.

3. He is the first Indian man to reach the finals of BWF World Championship.

Which of the above statement/statements are correct?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1 and 3.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• On December 19, 2021, **Kidambi Srikanth won a silver medal at the World Badminton Championships in Spain.**
 
• He has won silver at the **BWF Championships**, becoming the** first male shuttler to do so. (Hense Statement 1 is correct)**
 
• In the final, **Singaporean Loh Kean Yew** defeated him.
 
• With the silver medal, Srikanth now competes against past runners-up **P V Sindhu and Saina Nehwal.**
 
• **Loh has won the World Championships title**, becoming him the first guy from his nation to do so.
 
• He is the first man from India to advance to the BWF World Championship finals.
 
• India took home two medals from the **2021 World Championship**, with Lakshya Sen's bronze and **Srikanth's silver. **(Hense Statement 3 is correct)
 
• Kidambi Srikanth was conferred with the prestigious** Arjuna award in 2015 for Badminton. **(Hence Statement 2 is incorrect)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A badminton competition authorised by the **Badminton World Federation is called the World Badminton Championships (BWF).**
 
• The Badminton World Federation is the organisation in charge of overseeing badminton internationally.
 
 
• **Headquarters: Malaysia's Kuala Lumpur**
 
• **Established: 5 July 1934**
 
 
 
• **P.V. Sindhu** won the bronze medal in the women's singles competition at the** Tokyo Olympics** in August 2021.
 
• **Nandu Natekar**, a Badminton Legend and recipient of the **Arjuna Award,** passed away in July 2021.
